title: Retail sale price (maximum retail price)
requirement: The package must state a retail sale price. Only the presence of that declaration is checked here. Whether it is clearly indicated as the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency is part of the clause but is NOT tested.
legal_reference: Rule 6(1)(e) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
source_note: Checked 2026-08-30 by Claude Code (automated legal-source check) for raghavrrrao against the Department of Consumer Affairs (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution) consolidated publication 'Book on Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 with all amendments', https://consumeraffairs.gov.in/public/upload/admin/cmsfiles/whatsnews/Book_on_Legal_Metrology_Packaged_Commodities_Rules,2011_with_all_amendments_whatsnews.pdf (sha256 0ef948f9c6b89f5dfb20d384861901714fd0dc54fc67b5b86c772d2c3f983a4b; server Last-Modified 2025-04-14). Clause (e) reads there, verbatim: 'the retail sale price of the package;', followed by the words substituted vide G.S.R. 629(E) dated 23rd June 2017 w.e.f. 1.1.2018: 'shall clearly indicate that it is the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency:'. The source records that the illustrations and rounding words which followed were replaced by the words 'in Indian currency' vide G.S.R. 779(E) dated 2nd November 2021 w.e.f. 1.4.2022, now w.e.f. 01.10.2022 vide G.S.R. 226(E) dated 28th March 2022. Rule 2(m), as substituted vide G.S.R. 629(E), defines 'retail sale price' verbatim as 'the maximum price at which the commodity in packaged form may be sold to the consumer inclusive of all taxes'. Proviso (C) to rule 6(1) reads verbatim: 'no declaration as to the retail sale price shall be required to be made on (i) any package containing bidi; (ii) any domestic liquefied petroleum gas cylinder of which the price is covered under the Administrative Price Mechanism of the Government.' THIS RULE IS EVALUATED: the implemented check tests only that a retail sale price declaration is present, not that it is clearly indicated as the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency - see the _comment keys above and rules/SOURCES.md. HUMAN COUNTER-REVIEW BY A NAMED REVIEWER IS STILL OUTSTANDING.
_comment_2: STEP 2 ACTIVATION: the exemptions written into this clause are now expressed as applicability conditions on its RuleRequirement in rules/framework/rules.json, and apps.compliance.services.applicability resolves them from the facts declared for a submission BEFORE this validator runs. A package declared as one the clause excuses is recorded NOT_APPLICABLE, not as a violation. A package where the exempting fact was never declared reaches REVIEW_REQUIRED for this clause rather than a verdict. That is what makes activation safe; the categories are no longer the only lever.
_comment_3: The exemptions now carried on the requirement: proviso (C) for bidi and for domestic LPG cylinders priced under the Administrative Price Mechanism, and alcoholic beverages where State Excise Laws provide for the declaration.
_comment_4: PRESENCE ONLY, AND THIS ONE UNDER-CLAIMS THE MOST. Clause (e) requires the price to be 'clearly indicated as the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes in Indian currency'. That is a FORMAT requirement and no format check is registered, so only the presence of a retail sale price is tested. The requirement text below is narrowed to match; the full clause wording stays on the RuleRequirement in the framework.
